Best phone setup

Use this guide like an app — and keep it available offline.

1. Install this website

On Android, tap Install app below when available. On iPhone, open in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → turn on Open as Web App.

iPhone/iPad: Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen → Open as Web App.
2. Let links open Google Maps

The exact-pin and navigation buttons use Google’s universal Maps URLs. When the Google Maps app is installed, the phone normally opens the app automatically.

Test Avalanche Lake pin
3. Prepare for no signal

Download the Glacier area in Google Maps and save Glacier for offline use in the free NPS App before leaving Wi-Fi.

Google offline-map stepsNPS App instructions
Important: The installed guide and embedded photos can work offline after the first successful load, but external Google Maps and trail websites still need their own offline downloads. Use Google Maps for roads and exact pins; use NPS signage/current trail status for hiking.

Day 1 · West Glacier

Avalanche Lake & Lake McDonald

The strongest possible first day on the west side

Day 1 now begins at the exact trail access point

Park once at Avalanche Picnic Area, enter Trail of the Cedars, branch onto Avalanche Lake Trail, then finish the day at Lake McDonald Lodge and Apgar Beach.

Beauty
★★★★★
Effort value
★★★★★
Kid-friendly
★★★☆☆
Photos
★★★★★
Family plan: Avalanche Lake is the main outing: about 4.6 miles round trip. Start early, carry your child when needed, and turn around at Avalanche Gorge if the family is not comfortable continuing.

Places you will see, in order

  1. Avalanche Lake Trailhead → Avalanche Gorge → Avalanche Lake
  2. Lake McDonald Lodge and lakeside dock
  3. Apgar Village and Apgar Beach sunset

Illustrated route overview. Use the separate map buttons in each numbered location below for actual navigation.

Each location has its own Google Maps parking pin and final-scenery pin. Stops that share the same parking lot clearly say to leave the car there.

Day 3 · Northeast Glacier

Many Glacier & Grinnell Lake

The park’s grandest valley, made family-manageable

Many Glacier is organized by where the car stays

Park at Many Glacier Hotel for the hotel, Swiftcurrent Lake, boat tour, Lake Josephine, and Grinnell Lake. Move the car only for the optional Redrock Falls hike.

Beauty
★★★★★
Effort value
★★★★★
Kid-friendly
★★★★☆
Wildlife chance
★★★★★
Family plan: Reserve the boat early. The boat-assisted Grinnell Lake route gives the family major scenery with much less walking than Grinnell Glacier.
Current-status reminder: Many Glacier experienced a temporary flooding closure in June 2026. Because your trip is in September, recheck the live NPS conditions page before relying on this day. Check live NPS conditions.

  1. Many Glacier Hotel and Swiftcurrent Lake shoreline
  2. Many Glacier boat dock and Swiftcurrent Lake crossing

  5. Optional: Redrock Falls

Decision tool

Assign the days after checking the forecast.

Use Day 2. Logan Pass and the high road lose the most value in cloud. Protect the clearest day for them.
Use Day 1 or Day 4. Forest, gorge, and waterfall scenery still works under overcast skies.
Do not force alpine hiking. Use lodges, visitor centers, Lake McDonald shoreline, Trail of the Cedars, or a safe low-elevation drive. Recheck official road and trail status.
Live NPS conditionsTrail status
Wildlife & safety

Look, but never chase the sighting.

Logan Pass

Possible mountain goats, marmots, and bighorn sheep.

Many Glacier

Strong chance of seeing moose or bears at a safe distance.

St. Mary valley

Scan open slopes and lake edges in the morning and evening.

Non-negotiable: Carry accessible bear spray, hike together, keep the child within arm’s reach, make noise in limited visibility, and follow current NPS distance rules. Never approach an animal for a photo.
